what_it_does: Wireless power transfer (WPT) sends power through the air to battery-free implanted medical devices (pacemakers, neurostimulators). The rectifier converts the incoming AC signal to DC power. The problem: implants often need two different voltage levels—low voltage for the sensitive recording front-end (which wants stability) and high voltage for the stimulation back-end (which needs fast response). Cascading two rectifiers wastes power and space. This work achieves both voltages simultaneously within a single rectifier stage operating at 6.78 MHz, with independent control over each output.
